title: Ming-Image releases a 6B design model with RGBA output and an image-layer companion
author: siddhantfuture
selftext:
I’ve been looking at this more from the game-dev side, and the RGBA output is probably the most useful part for 2D assets.  
  
Design can generate things like UI elements and posters, while Design-Layer can take a finished graphic and split it into separate transparent pieces. That could be handy when you want to reuse or rearrange parts of an asset instead of generating everything again.  
  
The important limitation is that these are still raster images. It’s useful for asset creation, but it’s not the same as having a ready-made game asset pipeline.
